subject.title: [Feature]: Add optional capability descriptors to tool definitions

question: What canonical tool-capability taxonomy and trust semantics should OpenClaw expose to plugin policy, Gateway, and audit consumers?
rationale: This cannot be safely chosen by cleanup automation because the descriptor names and defaults become public security-policy facts and overlap several active capability, provenance, permission, and audit proposals.

options.title: Approve unified descriptor contract
options.body: Define additive optional descriptors with unknown-by-default semantics and thread them through tool definitions, plugin metadata, inventories, Gateway protocol, trusted policies, and before_tool_call payloads.

options.title: Fold into capability permissions
options.body: Keep this issue blocked behind the broader default-deny capability permission model so descriptor facts ship only with an enforceable grant subsystem.

options.title: Limit first consumer to Security Matrix
options.body: Let the Security Matrix/audit model establish the first vocabulary and defer a general public descriptor field until that contract lands.

recommendation.title: Approve unified descriptor contract
recommendation.body: Define additive optional descriptors with unknown-by-default semantics and thread them through tool definitions, plugin metadata, inventories, Gateway protocol, trusted policies, and before_tool_call payloads.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the closest host-hook and plugin metadata contract that this feature would extend.
